rules.why: Presenting a plan only keeps it waiting; the user approves it in the form.
Verify runs the unit's tests for an approved plan and keeps the receipt.
step_done makes its own checks (verify, files, secrets) before the harness commits.
The git block judges its command by the git rules itself and runs it only with the user's word where they ask.
A revision only waits for the user's approval again.
Dropping a waiting plan approves nothing; its revisions stay.
A skip gives up a step; its behaviours are kept skipped.
Settling ends only proven plans, or unproven plans of dead sessions after the user's Yes in a form.
git.commit judges its files by the plan, the verify and the commit guards itself.
git.push judges the push like git push in a shell, and refuses the home and protected branches.
A merge request opens only after the user confirms its full text in a form.
